sources.entry: Nullboard - Single-page minimalist kanban board; compact, highly readable and quick to use. (Demo) BSD-2-Clause Javascript

summary.one_liner: Nullboard is a minimalist, single-page kanban board and task list manager that stores all data locally in the browser and works offline.
summary.what_it_does: Nullboard is a single HTML file web app (with jQuery and a webfont pack) for organizing notes into lists on boards, in a compact kanban-style layout. Notes and lists are edited in place, changes save automatically, and the last 50 revisions are kept for undo/redo per board. Notes can be dragged between lists, collapsed to their first line, styled differently as section dividers, and lists can be reordered. Data is stored in localStorage and can be exported to or imported from a plain JSON text file. Optional automatic local backups are offered through separate companion tools: Nullboard Agent (native Windows app), Nullboard Agent Express Port (express.js portable app), and nbagent (Python, for Unix). The README also describes multiple boards, keyboard shortcuts including Tab navigation, recognized http/https links, and theme, font, and size settings.
use_cases: keeping local task lists without cloud storage
backing up board data to local disk
how_to_run: Open the single HTML file in a web browser (no server setup described in the README)
notable: Single HTML file app that works completely offline
All data kept in browser localStorage with JSON import/export
Undo/redo of last 50 revisions per board
Optional automatic local backups via companion Windows, Express, and Python agents
Keyboard-driven editing, including Tab navigation and CapsLock link highlighting
caveats: Explicitly marked as beta with no warranty
Designed for desktop keyboard and mouse; mobile and touch essentially untested
Browser support: Firefox and Chrome tested; Safari expected to work; Edge may work
Data lives in localStorage, so clearing the browser cache can lose data
summary.license: BSD-2-Clause with the Commons Clause (README states this; the Commons Clause restricts selling the software)
